starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: Ah, an adventurer. Could you spare some of your time to help me?

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: It's a sorry tale. I was once an accomplished sculptor, you see.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: I made statues for the kings, queens and rulers of Gielinor. But then there was the accident...

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: After that, I could never hold a chisel again.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: But I have been struck by my muse while travelling the desert, and want nothing more than to build a statue in this area.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: The desert's plain and full of sand, and needs more decoration.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.player: So, what would you need my help with?

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: As I said, I can't hold a chisel, but I can guide you in crafting the statue for me.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: I'd need you to quarry the stone for it, as well.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: Well, will you help me with my art?

steps.player: Of course!
You'll have to explain it to me as you go along, but count me in.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Excellent.

steps.player: What should I be doing to make your statue?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: There is a stone quarry nearby; I require several blocks of sandstone in order to make the statue.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Each of these blocks should be around... well, let's say thirty two kilograms for the first one.

steps.player: I can't mine a block that big!

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Well, then, bring me enough smaller blocks to make thirty two kilograms, and I will deal with it.

options.text: So, how much do different blocks of sandstone weigh?

steps.player: So, how much do different blocks of sandstone weigh?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: From what the last adventurer told me, there are tiny blocks that weigh 1 kg, small blocks that weigh 2 kg, and medium-sized blocks that weigh 5 kg.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: There are also large blocks that weigh 10 kg, but I doubt a weedy adventurer like you could even carry one, let alone mine one cleanly.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Apparently, the more skilled you are at mining, the larger the blocks you can chip off the rock.

options.text: Okay, I'll get on with it.

steps.player: Okay, I'll get on with it.

options.text: I don't know, that sounds like a lot of work.

steps.player: I don't know, that sounds like a lot of work.

steps.speaker: Lazim

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Try not to lose it, adventurer.

options.text: How do I get further into the temple?
Do you know where the statue's head is?

steps.player: Do you know where the statue's head is?

steps.text: If the player lost the stone head:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You didn't get far from here before you mislaid it.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: This time, try not to drop it.
If the player still has the stone heead:

steps.player: Do you know where the statue's head is?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: ...You're carrying it, adventurer.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Been at the Asgarnian Ale a little too much, have we?

options.condition: If the player doesn't have the left arm:
If the player doesn't have the right arm:
If the player doesn't have the left leg:
If the player doesn't have the right leg:

options.text: How do I get further into the temple?
Could you make these stone limbs easier to carry?

steps.player: Could you make these stone limbs easier to carry?
They're really heavy, and they weigh me down.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Of course not! I'm not a carnival conjurer.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Adversity builds character, adventurer. Heft them around by yourself.

steps.player: Oh, okay.

options.text: Do you know where the statue's head is?

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: If the player lost the right arm:

steps.player: I mislaid the statue's right arm.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: I suppose I'm useful to have around at these times. I found it when you dropped it around here.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: If the player lost the left arm:

steps.player: I can't find the statue's left arm.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: It's lucky for you that I notice these things. Here, you managed to drop it in this room.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: If the player lost the left leg:

steps.player: Er... I don't know where I put the statue's left leg.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You dropped it near the statue. Do I have to hold your hand through everything?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Here it is.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: If the player lost the right left:

steps.player: I lost the statue's right leg.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Well, it didn't go far - I found it in here. Take better care of it next time.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: You place the arm in the lock. It fits exactly.
A cutscene begins.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: At last, it's complete. A temple fit for my lord.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-take-si.text: You take the metal sigil. It's cold to the touch.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: You place the leg in the lock. It fits exactly.
A cutscene begins.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Knight
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: All right, men, destroy that evil sorceress... and her temple with her!

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: You will never have this temple - it belongs to my lord!
Enakhra casts a spell that kills three of the knights.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Knight
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: F-for Avarrocka!

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Ah ha ha ha ha!
Enakhra casts a spell that freezes the final knight.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Knight
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Aaaaaargh!
You place the arm in the lock. It fits exactly.
A cutscene begins.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Akthanakos
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Well, why would Zamorak want a temple? You said he needed weapons instead.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: I wish I'd never supported him.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Akthanakos
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: So you've seen sense? You'll join our side?

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Of course.
Akthanakos walks away and Enakhra laughs.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Heh heh heh...
You place the leg in the lock. It fits exactly.
A cutscene begins.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: Surely this would make a good weapon...
Enakhra casts a spell on some bones. A skeleton spawns, then turns back into bones.

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.speaker: Enakhra
bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-open-do.text: No, no! Curse it, that doesn't work!

bottom-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-placing.text: You place the sigil in the lock. It fits exactly.

options.text: How do I get further into the temple?
Do you know where the statue's head is?
Can you help me with this pedestal I've found?

steps.player: Can you help me with this pedestal I've found?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: What pedestal?

steps.player: It's on the floor above this. It looks sort of important.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Really? Did it have some sort of recess on the top?

steps.player: Now that you mention it, it did...

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: In that case, perhaps you should try using the head of the statue on it.

steps.player: Do you know where the statue's head is?

steps.text: If the player never got the statue's head:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Ah, it fell off when the statue dropped through the ceiling. I've been keeping it safe since then.
If the player still has the statue's head:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: ...You're carrying it, adventurer.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Been at the Asgarnian Ale a little too much, have we?
If the player lost the statue's head:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You didn't get far from here before you mislaid it.

options.text: How do I get further into the temple?
Do you know where the statue's head is?
Can you help me with this pedestal I've found?

steps.player: Can you help me with this pedestal I've found?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: What pedestal?

steps.player: It's on the floor above this. It looks sort of important.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Really? Did it have some sort of recess on the top?

steps.player: Yes, and I tried using the statue's head with it...
...but it didn't fit properly.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Hmm. Intriguing, adventurer.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Perhaps you should find out what shape the recess is, so you can sculpt something that will fit in it.

steps.player: Are you sure that will work?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Adventurer, I know more about this temple than you do.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: All you need to do is make a mould of the recess somehow, then use it as a guide to make another head.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: It should be made from the same granite as the statue's head was.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-s.text: You press the soft clay into the hollow, and make a positive mould of it.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-c.text: You carefully chisel the granite block to match the mould you made.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.text: You place the stone head into the hollow. It fits exactly.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.text: But it's still a nice temple, isn't it?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.text: Ha ha ha. You believed me, didn't you?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-t.text: I would never desert my lord!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Well done unlocking those doors, adventurer. Did you have any problems?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: I saw some really strange visions. Everything went grey...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Those are some of the traps to keep people away from this temple.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Thankfully, they didn't send you mad this time.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: That doesn't sound good.
So, are we at the top of the temple now?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: No, there is another floor above this. You have to go up a ladder in the room to the north.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Hah, that's easy. Treasure, here I come!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: There's a magic barrier in the way. And right now, it won't let anything through.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Oh...
Is there any other way to get upstairs?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: No, but I suspect the other rooms on this floor have magical properties. If you solve all the puzzles they present, then...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: How will I know when I've solved them?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Oh, it'll be quite obvious.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: The globes on the pedestal here will also light when you've solved the room they correspond to.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Have you come to torture me again?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Oh, you may look human, but I know you're not. I've heard stories.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: How you Mahjarrat can take on any form, and use magic to inflict pain without any weapons.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: I, er... what?
I have no idea what you're talking about, but I'm just as human as you are.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: You'll never get what you want from me. I'm a soldier of Avarrocka, and will stand strong!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Look, I'm not going to hurt you!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Besides, I am already wounded, and have been so for many years, thanks to this spell you cast on me. And hungry. So very, very hungry.

steps.player: I've got some food you can have. It's quite tasty.
Here, try this. It should fill you up.
Have some of this food. It's really good, I promise!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My daughter was learning to cook this when I left.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered her in so long... thank you for reminding me of her.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My son loved this dish. He would have eaten it every day if we had let him.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered him in so long... thank you for reminding me of him.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: A cake? There's nothing to celebrate, is there?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: So many years gone by. My children must have grown up and left home.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered them in so long... thank you for reminding me of them.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a baked potato:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Did you just dig that up and throw it into an oven?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It doesn't look good at all.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd prefer it with some sort of topping...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a baked potato with toppings:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: That doesn't look too bad at all.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It could almost be my wife's wonderful cooking.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered her in so long... thank you for reminding me of her.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you take me for? A rabbit?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a vegetable:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What's this? Did you just dig it out of the ground?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives cooked meat or fish:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you think I am, a bear? It's not even seasoned!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm a civilised man, not a barbarian gnawing on his kill!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Oh, how pleasant. I'm surprised you remembered to cook it after you killed it!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives something half-eaten:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm hungry, but not so hungry that I'll eat your leftovers.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: That's revolting! Why would you give people food you've already eaten half of?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm not touching that!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I might have enjoyed that food if you hadn't already eaten part of it.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: So, you're throwing scraps of food to me like I'm a dog, are you?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: If only you could feel the bite of my sword!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives gnome food:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Do you think I'm a gnome, or something? I'm not going to eat that!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives anything else he doesn't like:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What are you trying to feed me? I don't want that!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Are you just trying to feed me everything you have?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you take me for? A goat who'll eat whatever's in front of him?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives something inedible:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What are you trying to do, kill me?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Oh, I get it, you're experimenting on me with different things to see what I'll eat.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm not going to eat something your cat dragged in!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: After giving him something he rejected:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd rather have some good human home baking.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Some fresh home baking would be delicious.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd like something that's had some care put into making it.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd like to have a hearty meal fresh from the oven.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: The food you gave me healed my wounds, and it also reminded me of my family; that helped me to remember who I was.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: I'm afraid that I'm trapped here, but I still remember something of this floor of the temple.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If you need any hints about the rooms nearby, I can give you some help.

options.text: Tell me about the room with the fountain.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: When we came to the temple, that fountain was frosted with ice.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Even chipping at it with swords or lighting fires under it didn't do anything.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My guess is that some sort of magic is keeping it that way.

options.text: Tell me about the room with the furnace.

steps.player: Tell me about the room with the furnace.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I tried to go in there, but the smoke was so thick I could barely see the furnace.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It may be that it's blocked, in which case you'll have to clear it out.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: A good breeze should do the trick.

options.text: Tell me about the dark room.

steps.player: Tell me about the dark room.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I never went in there myself, but I peered through the door.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: There seemed to be fires of some sort all around the room, but they were burning low.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd imagine they've gone out by now.

options.text: It's okay, I don't need any help.

steps.player: It's okay, I don't need any help.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-cast-fi.text: With a hiss of steam, the ice melts away from the fountain.

steps.text: It looks like there was once a maple log fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a normal log fire burning here.
It looks like there was once an oak fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a candle burning here.
It looks like there was once a coal fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a willow log fire burning here.
You place the maple logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the oak logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the lit candle carefully in the brazier.
You place the coal in the brazier, and carefully light it.
You place the willow logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: Wind rushes through the furnace, clearing away what's blocking it.
The smoke clears from the room.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-pass-th.text: You walk through the barrier easily.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: The treasure's up ahead, adventurer. Be careful of the traps.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What traps?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Oh, I don't know. Perhaps, say, huge skeletons that'll tear your arms and legs off?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Nothing, adventurer, nothing. You just trot along and get that treasure, now.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Leave this temple at once, or I shall be forced to attack!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I will defend this door until I am released from this prison of bone...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: You shall not pass me, unless I crumble into dust!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: These bones that trap me will block your path!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Now, flee before I attack you!
The Boneguard attacks the player.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.speaker: Freed Spirit
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: Thank you, kind [sir/lady]... now I am free from my imprisonment.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.speaker: Freed Spirit
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: I no longer need these bones - take them, please, and bury what you can.
The spirit disappears with a soft sigh.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Don't interrupt me, human! I have to concentrate.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What are you doing?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: I'm keeping a weapon under control. If my attention wavers...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: ...then it tries to escape me. I must keep it safe for my lord Zamorak.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.text: Leave this place, before I am forced to attack!
If the player does not have protect from melee enabled:

steps.text: The Boneguard attacks the player once.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Someone so easy to hit isn't worth my time!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.text: If the player has protect from melee enabled:

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: If you value your life, young [man/woman/one], then flee!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: You should not be here! This is a dangerous place for beings such as you!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am impressed, young [man/woman/one]. You seem to have more resilience than those I have fought off before.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Perhaps, then, you could help me with my predicament?

steps.player: Why, what's wrong?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am trapped in this form against my will... it has been a long and painful struggle to even regain control over my own mind.

options.text: Who's trapped you in this form?

steps.text: Same as below from "Who's trapped you in this form?"

steps.player: Why did you attack me?
I didn't do anything to deserve it!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: As I said, I am trapped like this against my will.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am forced to defend the one who enslaved me from any harm, even though it disgusts me to do so!

steps.player: Who's trapped you in this form?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: SHE has. She was my rival before we came to this world, and supported that upstart Zamorak in his quest to be a god.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: It angers me to think at how she tricked me into slavery...

steps.player: Yes, I understand, but who is 'she'?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Her name is Enakhra, and she is the one who made this accursed temple and this boneguard that I am trapped in.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Now, since you show some interest in my situation, will you help me?

steps.player: Of course, I'll help you out. But first of all, do you have any treasure?
I, er, was just wondering...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Certainly, young [man/woman/one]. If you help me, I will give you a valuable amulet, and some of my knowledge.

steps.player: That's good enough for me. What do I have to do?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Enakhra keeps me trapped in this form with magic.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Her hold over me grew weaker over the years, and I began to build a wall to keep her trapped in her own temple forever.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Unfortunately, she has strengthened her spells lately, and I can no longer will myself to continue building.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I want you to finish building this wall, that we might seal her in this temple forever, where she cannot taint the world with her creations again.

steps.player: About this wall...

options.text: Where do I get the stone?

steps.player: Where do I get the stone?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: There is a pile of rubble nearby, made of blocks that have fallen from the walls and the ceiling over time.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I have been trapped here for several thousand years, after all...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: How do I build the wall?

steps.player: How do I build the wall?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Since the blocks are heavy, you will need to be quite strong in order to lift them up to the wall.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Once you have placed the stones up on the wall, you must trim them with a chisel so that they do not fall off when you place the next layer.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

steps.player: How long will it take?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I was not far from finishing, I must say. It will most likely only take you three loads to finish building it.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: Could you tell me more about Enakhra?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Enakhra?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: She is a coward, and a despicable traitor. She even supported Zamorak when he tried to become a god.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Of course, even though she built a temple for him, he didn't care, and she's been hiding here ever since.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: Could you tell me more about yourself?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about yourself?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I was once a proud mage, and now look at me. Trapped inside a bone skeleton and forced to defend my rival's temple.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: To think I believed her when she said she wanted to become allies and make amends for our rivalry!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: That two-faced, conniving, backstabbing wretch...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I suppose it is our nature, after all.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

steps.player: Okay, I'll start building.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Thank you. Once you are finished, the wall itself will shield me from most of her magic, and I will be free to move once more.

options.text: Of course, I'll help you out.

steps.text: Same as above from "Of course, I'll help you out. But first of all, do you have any treasure?"

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: So, you're determined to meddle in other people's business?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What do you mean?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: That weapon has suddenly become a lot harder to control.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: And I know it's your doing. He's tried to get you to help, hasn't he?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: If you're talking about Akthanakos, then yes!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Of course, I don't suppose he's told you who he's trying to support, has he?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Er, no. But if you hate him so much, I suppose he doesn't support Zamorak...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: How dare you throw around his name so casually?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: No, Akthanakos never supported Zamorak. Not even after these thousands of years...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: He has pledged his allegiance to someone much more foul.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Who?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: ...There are some names it is wiser not to mention, human.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Such as the name of my lord Zamorak, that you seem so fond of throwing around.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: But you said 'Zamorak' first!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Out of my sight, you unworthy scum, before I rend your flesh from your bones.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Never dishonour his name again.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Okay...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Well, adventurer, do you have the treasure yet?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: There doesn't seem to be any treasure there.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: None at all?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Hmm... the big skeleton promised to give me something if I helped him.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Ah ha! So, it's not attacking you? Well done, adventurer. Your second brain cell must be working overtime today.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-s.text: You add the stone to the wall.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-c.text: You trim the stone that was added to the wall.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: The wall's finally built!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for all your help.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: I can feel Enakhra's control over me fading. Finally, I can be free from this imprisonment...
The Boneguard turns into Akthanakos.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: After thousands of years... finally, I am no longer her slave.
If the player has no inventory space:

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: As thanks for your help, young [man/woman/one], please take this amulet of mine.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Wow. Er, what does it do?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It allows you to understand the speech of the Ugthanki, my patron animals, and other camels.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It is also bound to the desert, and can thus transport you back to this temple if you wish.
Continues with Enakhra cutscene.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: After thousands of years... finally, I am no longer her slave.
If the player has no inventory space:

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: As thanks for your help, young [man/woman/one], please take this amulet of mine.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Wow. Er, what does it do?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It allows you to understand the speech of the Ugthanki, my patron animals, and other camels.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It is also bound to the desert, and can thus transport you back to this temple if you wish.
Continues with Enakhra cutscene.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: After so many years, why didn't you just give up?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: Now my lord will punish you for destroying his weapon.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: Ha ha... in that case, I'm sure lord Zaros will be happy to intervene.
Akthanakos and Enakhra transform into skeleton forms.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: I'll be waiting for you in the north, Akthanakos.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: It'll be a pleasure to fight you once more...

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: Well, thank you, adventurer. You've just deprived me of a wonderful chance to learn from one of Zamorak's first followers.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.player: What? What about that treasure you were looking for?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: You utter imbecile! Did you think I was looking for gold?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: sigh* I might as well stay to study this temple. It has some interesting magical properties.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.player: Ooh, you're a mage? Can you teach me any spells?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: I'm sure I've dropped hints the size of Varrock, but you might not have noticed. I'm a Zamorakian mage.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: If you really want to learn my spells, you'll have to dedicate yourself to Zamorak.

steps.player: I couldn't do that!

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Then you won't be learning any of my spells.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Ha ha ha ha!

steps.player: You're not very nice, are you?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: What did you expect from a Zamorakian mage?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You really thought I would teach you my secrets just like that? Ha ha ha! You are a naive fool.

steps.player: That's not very nice of you.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: I'm a mage of Zamorak, after all. What else do you expect?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: How are you and your defective brain doing nowadays, adventurer?
If the player lost the camulet:

steps.player: I've lost the amulet that Akthanakos gave me.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You scatterbrained fool. You dropped it in here. Since you have no space to carry it, I can't give it back yet.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You really are an idiot, aren't you? You dropped it in here when you left. Try not to lose it next time.
Lazim returns the Camulet to you.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: I'm not very nice. If you want to see who ruined all of my plans, adventurer, just look in a mirror.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.player: Suit yourself. At least I got a nice amulet for my trouble.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: If the player unlocked unlimited charges:

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: And don't forget who gave it unlimited charges for you!

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: About that amulet - I might be able to improve it for you, for a fee. Have you got it with you?
If the player has the amulet in the bank:

steps.player: No, I don't have it on me at the moment. I must have stored it somewhere.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Of course you did. I bet you spend your life collecting junk, storing it, then complaining you've run out of storage space. Fetch the amulet if you want my help.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: If the player has the amulet:

steps.player: Yes, I've got it here.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Yes, it's what I thought. This amulet will run out of charges all the time, if you keep using it. For one million coins I can give it unlimited charges.

options.text: Why do you need so much money for it?

steps.player: Why do you need so much money for it?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Three reasons. Firstly, I'm a Zamorakian mage - we're not big on charity work. Secondly, I want the money. Finally, in case you need reminding, I hate you.
If the player doesn't have the coins:

steps.player: Right. Well, I haven't got that kind of money on me.
Okay, here's one million coins.
I'm not interested.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Your loss.

steps.player: Maybe another time.

18g95M.speaker: Lazim
18g95M.text: I'm now carrying [1-32] kg of your inexpertly-quarried stone.

hkR5tY.player: Why won't you take more than 32 kg of stone?

hkR5tY.speaker: Lazim
hkR5tY.text: Because, adventurer, I'm not going to carry more of your blocks than I absolutely must.

hkR5tY.speaker: Lazim
hkR5tY.text: If your blocks are too big, break them with a chisel or a pick.

bVVXnP.speaker: Lazim
bVVXnP.text: I'm now carrying [1-20] kg of your inexpertly-quarried stone.

s_fS9w.speaker: Akthanakos
s_fS9w.text: Honour demands that I reward you... and yet you have no room to carry my reward. Please, return when you can take it from me.
